question.leadin: This country's 1991 breakup was followed by a series of namesake ethnic conflicts that lasted ten years.
question.text: Name this now-defunct socialist country that included the modern-day countries of Croatia, Montenegro, and Serbia.
question.answerHtml: Yugoslavia (accept Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia ; or SFRY )
question.clue: This European country joined India, Indonesia, and Egypt to form the Non-Aligned Movement, marking a break from Soviet hegemony.

swap.text: In the US, the hardest ski runs are designated with one or two diamonds of this color.
swap.clue: This adjective described Pyotr Wrangel, who was nicknamed this type of baron, as well as staunch monarchist "Hundreds."

question.text: Princip also aligned himself with this secret Serbian military society, which had planted many would-be assassins throughout Sarajevo.
question.clue: Organized in four or five member committees, its undisputed leader was a man known as "Apis," and its activities were enthusiastically supported for a time by Crown Prince Alexander.

swap.leadin: A drone hovered over a soccer field with a flag of this country during a match, causing a fight between players from this country and Serbia.
swap.text: Name this Balkan nation that, in 1998, backed the Kosovo Liberation Army in its bid for independence. In 2014, it was granted candidate status for EU membership.
swap.clue: This home of Skanderbeg was ruled by the isolationist Enver Hoxha.

question.text: This general was the leader of Army of the Republika Srpska (serp-ska) and oversaw the massacre of Bosniaks at Srebrenica and the Siege of Sarajevo. This earned him the nickname the "Butcher of Bosnia."
question.clue: Of course, the Serbs were trying to do their own version of ethnic cleansing - this Serb was arrested on May 26, 2011 for war crimes including orchestrating the Siege of Sarajevo and the 1995 Srebrenica massacre.

swap.leadin: He kept himself in power and suppressed opposition with the Sigurimi police force.
swap.text: Name this Albanian communist leader, who led Albania through a period of industrialization in the latter half of the twentieth century.
swap.clue: This man was elected Prime Minister of Albania in 1944 and continued to rule until his death in 1985. He ushered in a period of communist rule in Albania that lasted until 1992.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the real-life Count Dracula, Vlad the Impaler.
question.text: While Vlad Dracula is commonly associated with Transylvania, he actually ruled over this region, which was combined with Transylvania and Moldavia to form the modern Romania.
question.clue: This region was the first one to be ruled by Michael the Brave.

swap.leadin: This ruler attempted to capture Mehmed II ("meh-MED the second") at the Night Attack of Targoviste ("tar-GOH-veesh-teh"), and subsequently was imprisoned by Matthias Corvinus ("mah-TY-as kor-VEE-nus").
swap.text: Name this Voivode ("VOY-voh-deh") of Wallachia ("wah-LAH-kee-uh") and brother of Radu the Handsome.
swap.answerHtml: Vlad the Impaler [or Vlad Tepes or Vlad III or Vlad Dracula; reject “Vlad Dracul”]
swap.clue: His younger brother Radu the Handsome spent most of his life as a hostage in Adrianople but returned to overthrow him in 1462, leading to his exile at the court of Matthias Corvinus until a later reconquest of Tirgoviste.

question.text: This 1878 treaty, which ended the Russo-Turkish War and was softened at the Berlin Congress, recognized the independenece of Serbia, Montenegro, Romania, and Bulgaria.
question.clue: The Berlin Conference of 1878 overturned this treaty between Russia and the Ottoman Empire, which established an independent Bulgaria and ended the Russo-Turkish War.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Ottoman incursions into Europe.
swap.text: Ottoman forces under Bayezid I routed Christian forces at the Battle of Nicopolis, which was fought at a fortress in this modern-day country. Basil II was known for slaying people of this country's namesake ethnicity.
swap.clue: The April Conspiracy targeted a leader of this country nicknamed "Bai Tosho."

question.text: The Hungarian Revolution was partially put down by Josip Jelacic ("YO-seep YAY-la-cheech"), a military leader of this ethnicity. Nationalists of this ethnicity formed the Ustase ("OO-stah-sheh") during World War II.
question.clue: People of this nationality received very little power over taxation in a dissatisfying agreement called the Nagodba, which did, however, allow them to elect their sabor.

swap.text: This Albanian hero left the Ottomans at the Battle of Nis. He later led his namesake rebellion against the Ottoman Empire, and also helped the Venetians in the First Ottoman-Venetian war before his death.
swap.clue: The Rilindja period of literary flourishment drew from that biography of this "Prince of the Epirotes" by Marin Barleti.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the start of World War I.
question.text: Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria and his wife were assassinated in this city, part of a region that Austria-Hungary had caused a crisis and an amendment of the Treaty of Berlin by annexing in 1908.
question.clue: According to a common myth, one event in this city took place while its perpetrator was eating a sandwich as a driver made a wrong turn.

swap.text: Benedetto Cotrugli, an economist from this city, described an early version of double-entry bookkeeping. This city became a major maritime republic after being transferred from Venice to Hungary in the Treaty of Zadar.
swap.clue: The nobles of this city elected its leaders to a position known as either Rector or knez ("k'nez").

question.leadin: According to angry Serbian nationalists on Youtube, this dynasty's king Uros the Weak was appropriately named, because he "did not kill Muslim, he did not kill foreigners."
question.text: Name this major Serbian dynasty of the Middle Ages, which lasted from 1166 to 1371.
question.clue: Stefan Dusan was a ruler from this Serbian dynasty, which lasted from 1166 to 1371. Founded in the principality of Raska by its namesake, its ruler Stefan the First-Crowned was recognized as king by Pope Honorius III while his brother Rastko was the first archbishop of an independent Serbian Orthodox Church.

swap.text: The legend that Elizabeth Bathory bathed in the blood of her virgin victims has led some to assign her vampiric qualities, calling her "Countess Dracula" in reference to this Wallachian prince who impaled many of his prisoners.
swap.answerHtml: Vlad III Dracula [or Vlad the Impaler; or Vlad Tepes]
swap.clue: This voivode of Wallachia who led the Night Attack against Mehmed II in 1462. He was captured by Matthias Corvinus of Hungary later that year.

question.text: The Great Power's ineffectual original choice for King of Albania, William of Wied ("VEED"), ruled from this city until the Congress of Lushnje ("LUSH-nyuh"). Lodewijk ("loh-deh-WIKE") Thomson died defending this city from Haxhi Qamili's ("HAH-jee CHYAH-muh-lee's") pro-Ottoman peasant revolt.
question.clue: Under Ottoman rule this city was a major market town in the Vilayet of Scutari, and in 1914 it became the capital of a kingdom led at the time by Prince William of Wied.

swap.text: Enver Hoxha, Ramiz Alia, Ed Cohn, and other leaders of Communist Albania stayed in power thanks to this secret police force that oppressed those whose ideology was deemed revisionist; it was at least nominally abolished in 1991.

question.text: This man came to power in the wake of Ceausescu's death. After riding to power on the wings of the anti-communist NSF, he served three non-consecutive terms as President of Romania.

swap.text: Later, Badinter promoted recognition of this country, in which he helped write the Ohrid Agreement. Under Zoran Zaev, this country signed the Prespa Agreement with its southern neighbor.
swap.answerHtml: North Macedonia [or Republic of Macedonia; or Makedonija; or Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia; or FYROM]
swap.clue: This nation's policy of "antiquization" included putting the "star of Vergina" on its flag in 1995, and erecting an equestrian statue of Alexander the Great in its capital city.
